issues.problem: dake-only explain: 'が and を are usually dropped after だけ' was ambiguous about position (they are omitted or follow だけ, never precede it).
issues.action: Reworded: left out, or can come after だけ (水だけを飲む), but never before it.

issues.problem: dake-only contrast vs ばかり: 'One single thing cannot take ばかり' contradicts 肉ばかり (a single kind of thing takes ばかり fine).
issues.action: Narrowed to 'a single individual or a one-off event'.

issues.problem: bakari-only explain: 'が and を drop before ばかり' was unclear and omitted that they may follow ばかり; 十日ばかり called 'old-fashioned' though it is still current in writing.
issues.action: Reworded to 'never come before ばかり: left out or follow it (肉ばかりを食べる)'; changed to 'literary; in conversation use ぐらい'.

issues.problem: bakari-only example English 'Please don't eat only sweet things all the time' was clumsy.
issues.action: Changed to 'Please don't eat sweet things all the time.'
